# EarnForge

> Developer toolkit for the LI.FI Earn API. Handles 23 integration pitfalls
> so you can focus on building yield products.

All figures below were verified against the live API on Aug 4, 2026:
711 vaults, 19 chains, 27 protocols, 68 vaults verification-flagged.

LI.FI rewrote the Earn API in April 2026. Every path moved, auth became
mandatory, and two documented field types are wrong in the current spec. If you
have older notes about this API, prefer this file — several of the things that
changed inverted rather than merely moved.

## Earn Data API (earn.li.fi)

Base URL: https://earn.li.fi
Auth: REQUIRED. Send `x-lifi-api-key`. Without it every endpoint returns 401.
Get a key from https://portal.li.fi.

Paths dropped the `/earn` segment in Apr 2026. `/v1/earn/vaults` is now
`/v1/vaults`, and the old paths return 404 rather than redirecting.

### GET /v1/vaults

List vaults with optional filters. Paginated, max 50 per page.

Query params:
- chainId (number) -- numeric chain ID, not chain name. e.g. 8453 for Base.
- asset (string) -- token symbol filter, e.g. "USDC"
- protocol (string) -- UNVERSIONED protocol id. "aave", not "aave-v3".
- minTvlUsd (number) -- minimum TVL in USD. NOT `minTvl`; see below.
- cursor (string) -- pagination cursor from the previous response's nextCursor

Unknown query params are dropped rather than rejected. Sending `minTvl` instead
of `minTvlUsd` returns HTTP 200 and the entire unfiltered fleet — 711 results
where the filter would have returned 41. A filter that fails open is worse than
one that throws, so spell the param exactly.

The same applies to protocol ids: a stale slug like `morpho-v1` returns HTTP 200
with `total: 0`, which is indistinguishable from a protocol that has no vaults.
Resolve ids from `/v1/protocols` rather than hardcoding them.

Response shape:
```json
{
  "data": [ ...vaults ],
  "nextCursor": "morpho:8453:_:0xbeef..." | null,
  "total": 711,
  "normalizedAt": "2026-08-04T14:03:50.453Z"
}
```

`nextCursor` is itself a vault slug.

### GET /v1/vaults/{chainId}/{address}

Get a single vault. chainId MUST be a number (e.g. 8453), not a chain name
(e.g. "Base"). Using a chain name returns 400.

### GET /v1/chains

List supported chains. Returns an array. Chain coverage changes; read the
endpoint rather than hardcoding a count.

### GET /v1/protocols

List supported protocols. Returns an array of objects with `id`, `name`, `url`.
The `id` is unversioned.

### GET /v1/portfolio/{walletAddress}/positions

Get earn positions for a wallet. The positions array is returned under `data`;
older responses used `positions`. Accept either.

## Composer API (li.quest)

Base URL: https://li.quest
Auth: REQUIRED. Send `x-lifi-api-key`. The same LI.FI key works for both
services, so one key is enough.

### GET /v1/quote

Get a deposit/swap/bridge quote. This is GET, not POST. POST returns 405.

Query params:
- fromChain (number) -- source chain ID
- toChain (number) -- destination chain ID (must match vault.chainId)
- fromToken (string) -- source token address
- toToken (string) -- MUST be vault.address (the vault share token), NOT the underlying token address
- fromAddress (string) -- wallet address
- toAddress (string) -- wallet address (same as fromAddress for deposits)
- fromAmount (string) -- amount in smallest unit (wei)
- slippage (number) -- optional, e.g. 0.03 for 3%
- fromAmountForGas (string) -- optional, amount to reserve for gas

Response includes transactionRequest (ready to sign), estimate (gas/fee costs,
execution duration), and action details.

## Vault object -- key field semantics

- address: the vault's share token address. This is what you pass as toToken to Composer.
- chainId: numeric chain ID (number, not string, not chain name)
- slug: "{protocolId}:{chainId}:_:{address}" -- e.g. "morpho:8453:_:0xbeef...".
  The old "{chainId}-{address}" form is gone. Code that splits on "-" to recover
  a chain id mis-parses every current slug, and since nextCursor IS a slug, this
  also breaks pagination.
- protocol: object with { id, name, url }. `id` is unversioned.
- isTransactional: boolean. If false, deposits via Composer will fail. 6.2% of the fleet.
- isRedeemable: boolean. If false, withdrawals may not be supported. 7.3% of the fleet.
- underlyingTokens: array of { symbol, address, decimals, priceUsd }.
- tags: array of strings (e.g. "stablecoin", "lst")
- depositPacks / redeemPacks: available deposit/redeem methods
- description: OPTIONAL, and usually absent — 76.8% of vaults omit it.
- verificationStatus: "none" | "flagged". UNDOCUMENTED — it appears in no spec,
  changelog or quickstart, and LI.FI's own hosted MCP server does not expose it.
  68 of 711 vaults (9.6%) are flagged. Sort by APY without checking it and a
  flagged vault lands at the top of your list.
- verificationStatusBreakdown: array of { reason, result }. Reasons seen live:
  "zero_apy" (most), "apy_outlier".

### analytics

- analytics.apy.total: number. ALREADY A PERCENTAGE. The spec says it is
  "expressed as a decimal (0.0534 = 5.34%)" and the official quickstart
  multiplies by 100. Both are wrong: following them renders a 29.19% vault as
  2919%.
- analytics.apy.base / analytics.apy.reward: the split of total.
- analytics.apy.reward is THREE-VALUED and the distinction is load-bearing:
  `null` means the protocol did not report (324 vaults), `0` means it reported
  none (300 vaults), and `> 0` means real incentives (87 vaults). Normalising
  null to 0 conflates 324 unknowns with 300 confirmed zeroes and destroys any
  reward-sustainability signal.
- analytics.apy1d / apy7d / apy30d: number OR null. Fresh vaults lack history.
- analytics.tvl.usd: NUMBER. The spec declares it a string. Accept both.
- analytics.updatedAt: ISO timestamp. The docs describe a 15-minute refresh; in
  practice the fleet updates in one hourly batch — 588 of 711 vaults share a
  single updatedAt minute — so the freshest reading is over an hour old and a
  tail runs to ~92 hours. Treat it as a coarse staleness signal.

Fields the OpenAPI spec documents that NO live vault sends: `caps`, `timeLock`,
`kyc`, `lpTokens`. Do not code against them.

## The pitfalls that invert

Most integration mistakes are things you have not done yet. These three are
things you may have already done correctly and must now undo:

1. Earn Data used to require no auth. It now hard-401s without `x-lifi-api-key`.
2. `analytics.tvl.usd` used to be a string. It is now a number.
3. Vault slugs used to be `{chainId}-{address}`. They are now
   `{protocol}:{chainId}:_:{address}`.

All 23 are documented at https://earnforge-docs.vercel.app/pitfalls/ with a
regression test each.

## EarnForge SDK

Install: npm i @earnforge/sdk

```typescript
import { createEarnForge, riskScore, isFlagged, parseTvl } from "@earnforge/sdk";

// One LI.FI key authenticates both Earn Data and Composer.
const forge = createEarnForge({ apiKey: process.env.LIFI_API_KEY });

// Auto-paginating vault iteration
for await (const vault of forge.vaults.listAll({ chainId: 8453 })) {
  if (isFlagged(vault)) continue;              // LI.FI flags 9.6% as suspect
  const risk = forge.riskScore(vault);
  console.log(vault.name, vault.analytics.apy.total, risk.label, risk.flags);
}

// Risk score: 7 dimensions, 0-10 composite. Labels are low >= 8, medium >= 6.
const risk = forge.riskScore(vault);
// { score: 9.7, label: "low", breakdown: {...}, flags: [] }

// Reward sustainability — preserves the null vs 0 distinction
import { rewardSustainability } from "@earnforge/sdk";
rewardSustainability(vault);  // "organic" | "incentive-heavy" | "unknown" | ...

// Build deposit quote
const quote = await forge.buildDepositQuote(vault, {
  fromAmount: "100",
  wallet: "0x...",
});

// Preflight checks before signing
const report = forge.preflight(vault, "0x...", { walletChainId: 8453 });

// Portfolio suggestions — excludes flagged vaults unless includeFlagged: true
const suggestion = await forge.suggest({
  amount: 10000,
  asset: "USDC",
  strategy: "conservative",
});

// Detect drift between the live API, LI.FI's OpenAPI spec, and our schemas
import { detectDrift } from "@earnforge/sdk";
```

## EarnForge CLI

Install: npm i -g @earnforge/cli

Requires `LIFI_API_KEY`. Every command supports `--json`.

```
earnforge list --chain 8453 --asset USDC --json
earnforge top --asset USDC --limit 5 --json
earnforge vault morpho:8453:_:0xbeef... --json
earnforge compare morpho:8453:_:0xbeef... aave:1:_:0x9277... --json
earnforge risk morpho:8453:_:0xbeef... --json
earnforge apy-history morpho:8453:_:0xbeef... --json
earnforge portfolio 0xwallet... --json
earnforge suggest --amount 10000 --asset USDC --strategy conservative --json
earnforge quote --vault morpho:8453:_:0xbeef... --amount 100 --wallet 0x... --json
earnforge simulate --vault morpho:8453:_:0xbeef... --amount 100 --wallet 0x... --json
earnforge withdraw --vault morpho:8453:_:0xbeef... --amount 100 --wallet 0x... --json
earnforge preflight --vault morpho:8453:_:0xbeef... --wallet 0x... --json
earnforge allowance --token 0x... --owner 0x... --spender 0x... --amount 1000000 --chain 8453 --json
earnforge approve --token 0x... --spender 0x... --chain 8453 --json
earnforge watch --vault morpho:8453:_:0xbeef... --json
earnforge chains --json
earnforge protocols --json
earnforge doctor --vault morpho:8453:_:0xbeef... --json
earnforge init my-yield-app
```

## EarnForge MCP server

Hosted, zero install, MCP revision 2026-07-28:

  https://earnforge-mcp.papermind-ai.workers.dev/mcp

12 tools, each with an outputSchema and validated structuredContent:
get-earn-vaults, get-earn-vault, get-earn-chains, get-earn-protocols,
get-earn-portfolio, get-vault-risk, quote-vault-deposit, quote-vault-redeem,
check-allowance, suggest-allocation, run-doctor, check-api-drift.

Every tool is annotated readOnlyHint / destructiveHint:false — quote tools
return unsigned transactions and nothing here signs or broadcasts. Pass your own
`x-lifi-api-key` header to use your own rate-limit budget.

The Agent Skill is also served over the same connection as MCP resources under
`skill://earnforge/*`.

## EarnForge Agent Skill

  npx skills add FarseenSh/earnforge

Follows the Agent Skills specification. Declares `LIFI_API_KEY` as a required
credential.

## Other packages

- @earnforge/react -- 11 hooks on wagmi + TanStack Query
- @earnforge/skill -- the Agent Skill as an npm package
